name: PulseGrid Agent Mesh
tagline: Eight AI agents that keep Indian road-freight corridors safe, unspoiled and moving.
description: PulseGrid is an agentic layer for India's freight and mobility corridors. A GRIDMASTER orchestrator decomposes a free-form request, dispatches specialist agents in dependency order, feeds each agent's result into the next, enforces guardrails, and stops at a human gate before public-facing or above-threshold actions. Eight specialists cover road-surface defects and municipal SLA, disruption-aware rerouting, cold-chain shelf life, driver welfare, emergency corridor pre-emption, multimodal handovers, carbon accounting and tamper-evident evidence. Every step and tool call is recorded in a replayable run.
problem_statement: India's road-freight and mobility corridors kill and waste at scale. In 2024 there were 4,87,707 road accidents and 1,77,175 deaths — about 20 deaths every hour — with over-speeding behind 70.3% of fatalities and potholes, curves and steep grades behind 13.8% of all accidents. Separately, 6.02–15.05% of fruit and 4.87–11.61% of vegetables are lost before reaching a buyer, and transport is the single largest loss stage. Logistics costs India ₹24 lakh crore a year (7.97% of GDP).
solution_summary: A mesh of eight agents, coordinated by GRIDMASTER, that reasons over costed options, acts through 23 instrumented tools, respects hard guardrails, and stops for a human before irreversible or public-facing actions. It runs on the fleets, phones and signals India already has — no new capital expenditure.

agent_endpoint_contract.request: { "request": "A vaccine truck is heading to Kochi and there is a flood on NH-544", "context": { "driver_id": "D-3310", "driver_language": "ml-IN" } }
agent_endpoint_contract.response: plan (intents, rationale, confidence) + full replayable reasoning trace + actions taken + outcome metrics + approval gates + evidence hashes

pricing.note: Open source under MIT. Free to run; the prototype uses no paid external services.

capabilities: Disruption-aware freight rerouting around floods and closures, with costed trade-offs
Cold-chain shelf-life modelling with automatic diversion before spoilage
Road-surface defect detection driving a municipal repair SLA
Emergency corridor pre-emption across signalised junctions
Driver fatigue monitoring with enforced rest and vernacular voice alerts
Carbon accounting and lower-carbon mode options
Tamper-evident evidence anchoring and paperless contract clauses
Multilingual output: English plus 22 Indian languages, with speech

impact.time_saved: Emergency pre-emption saves ~55 s per junction; 8 junctions ≈ 7 minutes per emergency run.
impact.cost_reduced: One prevented cold-chain rejection ≈ ₹3.4 lakh of cargo preserved (computed live in the prototype).
impact.accessibility: Driver alerts in the driver's own language — English plus 22 Indian languages, with speech output.
impact.verification: 17 outcome assertions run live in the dashboard and in CI; 33 assertions in the agent test suite.

compliance.network_egress: None required — all tools are local and deterministic simulators are labelled.
compliance.disclosure: Tools that would call an external service (vision scoring, weather feed, ULIP track-and-trace, ledger) are deterministic simulators, labelled `simulated` in every trace. Routing, the shelf-life model, fatigue scoring, carbon maths and evidence hashing are real computation.
